meta.pos: noun; noun; noun; noun; verb; verb; verb; verb

defs.def: the amount of money that you need in order to buy, make or do sth 费用；花费；价钱

ex.s: Library Type Loan Cost Article/Chapter Cost
ex.t: 图书馆类型 借阅费用 文章/章节费用

ex.s: It is becoming more costly.
ex.t: 它的花费越来越高。

ex.s: The reduction of cost in designing drones.
ex.t: 设计无人机成本的降低。

ex.s: Bring down the cost of labor.
ex.t: 降低劳动力成本。

ex.s: Chances are the cost will be a lot less than the cost of one bedroom.
ex.t: 很可能费用会比一间卧室的花费少得多。

ex.s: That includes huge savings in maintenance costs and better protection of railway personnel safety.
ex.t: 这包括维护成本的大幅节省和对铁路人员安全的更好保护。

ex.s: Last year, the couple’s daughter started a GoFundMe to help cover the costs of some materials and tools.
ex.t: 去年，这对夫妇的女儿发起了一个GoFundMe众筹，帮助支付一些材料和工具的费用。

defs.def: the total amount of money that needs to be spent by a business 成本

ex.s: The rising labor cost of building solar farms.
ex.t: 建设太阳能农场的人工成本上升。

ex.s: These lights, known as adaptive signals, have led to significant declines in both the trouble and cost of travels between work and home.
ex.t: 这些被称为自适应信号的灯，使上下班通勤的麻烦和成本都显著下降。

ex.s: To cut the cost of e-space protection.
ex.t: 降低网络安全保护成本。

ex.s: To reduce the cost of minerals.
ex.t: 为了降低矿产成本。

ex.s: There' s nothing very complicated about this usage, a budget line is one of the lines in the budget, with the service or good to be purchased named and the cost quantified,
ex.t: 这种用法并不复杂，预算线就是预算中的一条线，注明要购买的服务或商品并量化成本，

ex.s: adaptation is an ever-changing processB. the cost of adaptation varies with time
ex.t: 适应是一个不断变化的过程B. 适应的成本随时间变化

ex.s: But as we’ve reshaped the world around us, dramatically reducing the cost and effort involved in obtaining calories, we still have the same brains we had thousands of years ago, and this mismatch is at the heart of why so many of us struggle to resist tempting foods that we know we shouldn’t eat.
ex.t: 但当我们重新塑造周围的世界，大幅降低获取卡路里所需的成本和努力时，我们仍然有我们几千年前拥有的同样的大脑，这种不匹配现象正是我们许多人努力抵制诱人的食物的核心，而我们知道我们不应该吃这些食物。

ex.s: To reduce its running costs.
ex.t: 为了降低运营成本。

ex.s: The cost of making "Apes."
ex.t: 制作《猿》的成本。

ex.s: To figure out how much power these devices are using, Callie Babbitt and her colleagues at the Rochester Institute of Technology in New York tracked the environmental costs for each product throughout its life — from when its minerals are mined to when we stop using the device.
ex.t: 为了弄清楚这些设备用了多少电，纽约罗彻斯特理工学院的 Callie Babbitt 和她的同事们追踪了每种产品整个生命周期的环境成本——从矿物开采到我们停止使用该设备为止。

ex.s: This is why, in part at least, the US National Climate Assessment says that: ＂There is no ‘one-size fits all’ adaptation.＂ Nevertheless, there are some actions that offer much and carry little risk or cost.
ex.t: 这就是为什么，至少部分地，美国《国家气候评估》说：“没有‘一刀切’的适应。”尽管如此，有些行动收益大、风险和成本却小。

ex.s: To cut production costs.
ex.t: 为了降低生产成本。

defs.def: the effort, loss or damage that is involved in order to do or achieve sth （为做某事涉及的）努力，代价，损失

ex.s: But something inside me was going to climb that mountain at all cost． I could hardly wait to try this adventure again．
ex.t: 但我内心有股力量要不惜一切代价去爬那座山。我迫不及待地想再试一次这次冒险。

ex.s: Modernity is usually achieved at the cost of elegance.
ex.t: 现代性通常是以优雅为代价来实现的。

ex.s: While regularly eating out seems to   61  (become) common for many young people in recent years, it’s not without a cost.
ex.t: 尽管近年来经常在外就餐对许多年轻人似乎___61___（become）平常，但这并非没有代价。

ex.s: There could be an even   63   (high) cost on your health.
ex.t: 对你的健康可能有更___63___（high）的代价。

ex.s: Do we really recognise what it costs us as a society when children can’t move safely around our communities?
ex.t: 当孩子无法在我们的社区安全出行时，我们作为社会究竟意识到这让我们付出了什么代价吗？

ex.s: We invest a lot in roads that help us rush through, but we fail to account for the true costs.
ex.t: 我们投入巨资修建让我们匆匆穿行的道路，却忽略了真正的代价。

defs.def: the sum of money that sb is ordered to pay for lawyers, etc. in a legal case 诉讼费用
if sth costs a particular amount of money, you need to pay that amount in order to buy, make or do it 需付费；价钱为

ex.s: You like going to the movies and reading crime novels and you have $ 150 to spend, In the example below, assume that each movie costs $10 and each crime novel costs $15.
ex.t: 你喜欢看电影和读犯罪小说，有150美元可花。在下面的例子中，假设每部电影10美元，每本犯罪小说15美元。

ex.s: Assume that each movie costs 10 and each crime novel costs, $15, you have $150.Which is RIGHT according to this passage?
ex.t: 假设每部电影10元，每本犯罪小说15元，你有150元。根据这篇文章哪项是对的？

ex.s: But they cost $18!
ex.t: 但它们要18美元！

ex.s: He said that one of the boxes generated around $13,500 in revenue a month and cost only about $400 to rent.
ex.t: 他说，其中一个电话亭每月产生约13,500美元的收入，而租金仅需约400美元。

ex.s: Since crime novels in the example cost $15 and you have $150 available, if you spend all the available money crime novels, you can buy 10.
ex.t: 由于示例中的犯罪小说售价为$ 15 ，而您可以使用$ 150 ，因此如果您花费所有可用的货币犯罪小说，则可以购买10本。

ex.s: It’s expected to cost $279,000.
ex.t: 预计售价为27.9万美元。

ex.s: It’s expected to cost $279,000.And it won’t help if you’re stuck in traffic.
ex.t: 它预计售价为279,000美元。而且如果你遇到交通堵塞，它也无济于事。

ex.s: He soon reached his first target of $70, but when he gave the money to a charity, he was told that it actually cost $2,000 to build a well.
ex.t: 他很快达到了70美元的第一个目标，但当他把钱捐给慈善机构时，被告知打一口井其实要2000美元。

ex.s: If movies cost $ 10 each, then the maximum number of movies you can see with the money available is 15.
ex.t: 如果每部电影10美元，那么用可用资金最多能看15部电影。

ex.s: If the consumer needs an amount of A costing 0.75, she can then spend only 0.25 X, the amount remaining, on her purchase of B.
ex.t: 如果消费者需要花费0.75美元的A金额，那么她只能花0.25 X，剩下的金额用于购买B.

ex.s: The（2）     moment was quickly followed by mental math． How much time and money would it cost to replace the（3）     of that little wallet？ The credit cards， the driver's license， the cash， all lost to the bus．
ex.t: （2）____的那一刻紧接着便是心算。更换那个小钱包里的（3）____需要花费多少时间和金钱？信用卡、驾照、现金，全都落在了公交车上。

ex.s: They cost more to use at home.
ex.t: 它们在家中使用成本更高。

ex.s: You don't need expensive equipment; even the ball doesn't have to cost much money.
ex.t: 你不需要昂贵的设备；甚至连球都不需要花多少钱。

defs.def: to cause the loss of sth 使丧失；使损失

ex.s: She tried to pull the shoe back on, but it cost her precious time.
ex.t: 她试图把鞋穿回去，但这耗费了她宝贵的时间。

ex.s: This brief visit with Mother Nature cost me two days off from work, recovering from a bad case of sunburn and the doctor’s bill for my son’s food poisoning.
ex.t: 这次与大自然的短暂接触让我请了两天假，还因为严重的晒伤和儿子食物中毒的医药费而恢复了好一阵子。

defs.def: to involve you in making an effort or doing sth unpleasant 使付出努力；使做不愉快的事
to estimate how much money will be needed for sth or the price that should be charged for sth 估算成本；估价
